cards.title: Your health data has rights. So do you.
cards.body: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the DPDP Act, sets rules for how organisations handle personal data. Health information you share is personal data too.

cards.title: Consent comes first
cards.body: Apps and services generally need your clear consent to process your personal data. Consent should be specific, and you can withdraw it later.

cards.title: Used only for the stated purpose
cards.body: Data collected for one purpose should be used for that purpose. A reminder app shouldn't quietly turn your prescriptions into something else.

cards.title: Access, correct, erase
cards.body: You can ask what personal data a company holds about you, ask it to fix mistakes, and ask it to erase your data, unless the law requires it to be kept.

cards.title: Complain if something goes wrong
cards.body: Companies must offer a way to raise grievances. If that doesn't resolve it, the law sets up a Data Protection Board. Read the privacy policy before tapping agree.

takeaway: Under the DPDP Act you give consent, data serves the stated purpose, and you can access, correct, erase and complain.
share: Your health data has rights in India: consent, access, correction, erasure, and a way to complain.
